The state "this board has no such bus" was kept in two ways: Ex_I2C stayed
at its initial port -1 when the pin table had no external pins, and In_I2C
was set to port I2C_NUM_MAX when the board had no internal pins. M5GFX
takes a negative port as a software I2C port, so begin(), scanID() or any
transfer on such an Ex_I2C (for example M5.Ex_I2C.begin() in a sketch, or
M5.Rtc.begin(&M5.Ex_I2C)) used the pins that software port last used;
after board detection those are the internal I2C pins. And isEnabled(),
defined as port >= 0, returned true for In_I2C at I2C_NUM_MAX, so
M5.begin() looked for the internal RTC / IMU on a bus that does not exist.

isEnabled() now returns true only when setPort() / begin() gave the bus
valid SDA / SCL pins, and every I2C_Class call (begin, release, start /
restart / stop, read / write, the register helpers, scanID) returns false
(readRegister8: 0) without touching the bus when it is false. The Ex_I2C
checks in M5.begin() use isEnabled() instead of their own pin and port
test. A bus set up on a negative (software I2C) port with valid pins is now
enabled as well.

On the PC build, In_I2C / Ex_I2C are never set up, so begin() now returns
false there instead of the SDL stub's true.
